title: Syntheses, Structures, and Properties of Novel Cagelike Complexes Based on Dodecanuclear Lanthanide with a Large Cavity

synthesis.procedure: Na3H2L (0.5 mmol, 0.232 g) was added as a solid to an ethanol–water (1:1) solution (20 mL) of La(NO3)3·6H2O (1.0 mmol, 0.433 g) under stirring. The resulting suspension was refluxed for ca. 1 h. Aqueous NaOH (1 M) was added dropwise until the precipitate dissolved and the pH was adjusted to 8–9. After two weeks of evaporation at room temperature, block-shaped crystals suitable for X-ray analysis formed.

reagents.name: sodium hydroxide
reagents.amount: 1 M aqueous solution, dropwise to pH 8–9

synthesis.temperature: reflux ca. 1 h, then room-temperature evaporation
synthesis.time: reflux ca. 1 h; crystallization two weeks
synthesis.vessel_or_method: stirring and reflux in ethanol–water (1:1, 20 mL), then slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: precipitate dissolved by dropwise 1 M NaOH; block-shaped crystals isolated after two weeks of evaporation at room temperature

synthesis.procedure: Prepared analogously to 1: Na3H2L was mixed with Pr(NO3)3·6H2O (1.0 mmol, 0.435 g) in ethanol–water (1:1) under stirring and reflux (ca. 1 h). Aqueous NaOH (1 M) was added to dissolve the precipitate and adjust pH to 7–8. Block-shaped crystals formed by slow evaporation over two weeks.

properties.summary: Variable-temperature χMT of 2 decreases smoothly from 19.01 cm3 K mol−1 at room temperature (slightly below 19.2 cm3 K mol−1 expected for 12 isolated Pr3+ ions, 3H4, g = 4/5) on cooling to 5 K under 1 T. Antiferromagnetic Pr–Pr coupling cannot be deduced because of strong spin–orbit coupling; the decrease is attributed to thermal depopulation of crystal-field Stark levels of 3H4.

measurements.conditions: room temperature; 5–300 K, applied field 1 T; SQUID MPMS-7

properties.summary: Variable-temperature χMT of 3 is 19.62 cm3 K mol−1 at room temperature (slightly below 19.68 cm3 K mol−1 expected for 12 isolated Nd3+ ions, 4I9/2, g = 8/11) and decreases smoothly on cooling to 5 K under 1 T. Antiferromagnetic Nd–Nd coupling cannot be deduced because of strong spin–orbit coupling; the decrease is attributed to thermal depopulation of crystal-field Stark levels of 4I9/2.
